From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nimbuscloud.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, Aug 3, 2028 at 3:12 PM PDT
Subject: NimbusCloud downstream subcontractor clause & DPA alignment

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — quick heads up from procurement/legal as we start the SOW/order form finalization for the Nimbus integration (DEAL-7642). We plan to engage LogStream (logstream.io) to handle structured telemetry ingestion for this customer deployment. Nimbus requires:

- a subprocessor flow-down clause in your MSA/order form that obligates downstream vendors to comply with the DPA terms;
- an executed DPA that includes audit rights and an evidence list for SOC2/ISO; and
- an explicit callout that subcontracting does not reduce Redwood's obligations to Nimbus.

Attached are the current SOW and a short note with required DPA clauses (Nimbus_SOW_v2.docx, NIMBUS_DPA_Required_Clauses.pdf). Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood accepts flow-down to LogStream (or whether we need a separate subproc consent plus attestation)? If you prefer, we can accept your redline to our DPA instead of starting from our template.

Timing: Nimbus is aiming for signature week of Aug 14; they need subproc confirmation and DPA language by Aug 8 to hit internal gating.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of who on your side will handle the review and whether Redwood needs LogStream's SOC2 evidence upfront.

Best,
Tom

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, Aug 4, 2028 at 07:18 AM PDT
Subject: RE: NimbusCloud downstream subcontractor clause & DPA alignment

Hannah / Laura —

Thanks for flagging. Quick read-through and proposed approach below. High-level: we can accept flow-down to LogStream but should do it under an explicit subprocessor consent + narrow SOW amendment that: (a) requires LogStream to execute Redwood's subprocessor appendix (we can accept equivalent certs if we receive evidence), (b) preserves Redwood's liability cap and indemnity structure but lists an explicit carve-in for willful misconduct / breach of data obligations, and (c) clarifies audit rights (reasonable remote audit + right to request SOC2 / penetration test reports).

Specific recommended redlines (to be incorporated into NIMBUS_DPA_Redline.pdf):
- Subcontracting/Flow-Down: "Customer acknowledges that Redwood may engage subprocessors to perform Services. Redwood will (i) ensure that any subprocessors are bound by written agreements that impose obligations no less protective of Customer Data than those set forth in this DPA, and (ii) remain responsible for the acts and omissions of such subprocessors to the same extent Redwood would be liable for its own acts and omissions."

- Evidence & Audit: "Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide evidence of applicable certifications for any named subprocessor (e.g., SOC2 Type II). Reasonable audit rights shall be limited to (i) remote review of third-party certification reports and (ii) one on-site audit per 12 months subject to confidentiality terms; Redwood will not be required to provide source code or internal development repositories."

- Liability and Carve-ins: keep existing liability cap but carve out willful misconduct and breaches of Customer Data obligations from the cap. For subcontractor-caused breaches, Redwood remains first-responder and will pursue contractual remedies against the subprocessor.

- Order Form/SOW insertion: a short flow-down clause: "Any subcontractor engaged for this Order Form in connection with data processing shall be bound by the DPA and flow-down obligations. Redwood will notify Customer of the identity of any such subcontractor at least 10 days prior to disclosure of Customer Data and provide certification evidence upon request."

- Transition/Termination: include an option for Customer to require replacement of a subprocessor if reasonable security concerns are identified and Redwood cannot remediate within 30 days.

Operational ask: we should request LogStream's SOC2 Type II report or their auditor's contact for a bridge letter. If LogStream cannot provide that quickly, we can accept a signed subprocessor annex plus an attestation of controls for the short term.

I will draft the DPA redline now and share as NIMBUS_DPA_Redline.pdf. Laura — if you can draft the one-page SOW amendment (two bullets) we can attach and send to Tom.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts

Tom — thanks for the clear frame and timeline. Please find attached our redlines and the one-page SOW amendment for the Order Form. Key points:

- Flow-down: Redwood will accept flow-down to LogStream subject to (i) execution of Redwood's subprocessor appendix by LogStream or provision of an equivalent SOC2 Type II report, and (ii) Redwood remaining contractually responsible for subprocessor acts/omissions as described in our redline.
- Audit evidence: we will provide remote copies of SOC2/ISO reports; on-site audits are limited and subject to confidentiality and timing windows.
- Liability: we preserve the baseline liability cap but carve out willful misconduct and data-breach obligations. In the event of a subprocessor-caused breach, Redwood will lead the response and pursue remedies against the subprocessor.
- Timing: we can return an executed DPA (redlined) by Aug 7 provided we receive LogStream's SOC2 evidence or a signed subprocessor annex by Aug 6.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Nimbus accepts the SOW amendment we attached (Nimbus_SOW_v2_Redline.docx).
2) If Nimbus requires LogStream to execute a separate attestation to Nimbus, let us know — otherwise, we'll request LogStream's SOC2 and provide it to Nimbus directly.
3) If acceptable, we'll send the redlined DPA for signature via DocuSign (link to follow).
